docs.text:
Modern API gateways, microservices, and web applications face an impossible security trade-off:

docs.title: 1. Architectural Separation: Hot Path vs. Offline Control Plane
docs.text:
A core engineering principle of SATGuardian Edge WAF is the strict separation between in-path request evaluation (which must execute in microseconds with predictable latency) and out-of-band rule optimization (which performs 128-variable algebraic boolean minimization asynchronously via EXACTOR GXOR).

Subsystem Execution Path Implemented Algorithm Computational Complexity Measured Latency Lexical Decoder & Tokenizer In-Path (Edge WAF) Iterative URL/HTML decoding + comment stripping + token scan (src/ast/lexer.rs) \(O(L)\) where \(L\) is payload byte length ~6–10 µs (Rust) Bitmask Rule Evaluator In-Path (Edge WAF) 128-bit FeatureVector bitwise comparison (src/engine/sat_solver.rs) \(O(R)\) bitwise operations (\(R \le 64\) rules) ~4–6 µs (Rust) Total Edge Hot Path In-Path (Edge WAF) Combined Lexer + Bitmask Evaluator Linear in payload size, constant per rule 13.60 µs p50 / 14.53 µs avg EXACTOR GXOR Boolean Minimizer Out-of-Band (Cloud / Advisor) Differential Gray Code Mapping + {AND, OR, NOT, XOR} reduction (exactor-core-v128) \(O(\text{term\_count})\) linear scaling up to 128 vars 10–250 ms (Background) Digital Twin Verifier Out-of-Band (satguardian-advisor.py) Historical replay over benign SQLite ledger (waf_ledger.db) \(O(N_{\text{benign}})\) ~50 ms for 1,663 benign logs

Important Clarification: SATGuardian does not execute an NP-complete backtracking SAT solver (such as DPLL or CDCL) on the live HTTP request path, nor is it limited by the 20–30 variable exponential ceiling of classical Quine-McCluskey. Out-of-band logic minimization is powered by EXACTOR GXOR, which simplifies up to 128 Boolean variables (u128) over {AND, OR, NOT, XOR} and compiles the reduced invariants into u128 bitmasks for single-cycle bitwise evaluation on the edge.

docs.title: 2. Stage 1: Multi-Pass Lexical Normalization (src/ast/lexer.rs)
docs.text:
Attackers frequently evade traditional signature WAFs by nesting encodings (e.g., double or triple URL encoding ..%25252f, HTML entity encoding, or inline SQL comments /**/).

SATGuardian's lexer (Lexer::normalize_and_tokenize) applies a bounded, deterministic normalization pipeline before extracting grammatical tokens: 1. Iterative Percent-Decoding: Unwinds nested URL encodings up to a fixed recursion bound so obfuscated sequences resolve to their canonical ASCII characters. 2. Comment & Whitespace Canonicalization: Strips inline C/SQL comments (/* ... */) and collapses redundant whitespace so UNION/**/ALL/**/SELECT normalizes cleanly. 3. Contextual Token Extraction: Scans the normalized stream to identify structural tokens across five security domains ("Certainty Islands"): - ISLAND-SQLI: Quote delimiters, boolean tautologies ('1'='1', 1=1), UNION SELECT projections, stacked DDL (; DROP TABLE), and time-delay primitives (SLEEP, WAITFOR DELAY, BENCHMARK). - ISLAND-XSS: Executable <script> blocks, inline DOM event handlers (onerror=, onload=), <svg/onload>, and javascript:/data: pseudo-protocols. - ISLAND-RCE: Shell chaining operators (;, |, &&, `, $()) coupled with system binaries (cat, whoami, bash, curl, powershell) or dynamic evaluation sinks (os.system, eval(), subprocess). - ISLAND-LFI: Directory traversal sequences (../, ..\) and direct kernel/system file descriptors (/etc/passwd, /proc/self/environ, win.ini). - ISLAND-SSRF: Internal cloud metadata targets (169.254.169.254), loopback addresses (127.0.0.1, localhost), and non-HTTP proxy schemes (gopher://, dict://, file://).

docs.title: 3. Stage 2: 128-Bit Feature Vector & Bitmask Evaluation (src/ast/features.rs, src/engine/sat_solver.rs)
docs.text:
During inspection, extracted lexical properties and HTTP metadata are packed into a 128-bit integer (FeatureVector(pub u128)):

// Fast O(1) bitwise evaluation of a compiled rule cube against the request minterm
#[inline(always)]
pub fn matches_minterm(minterm: u128, required_mask: u128, expected_bits: u128) -> bool {
    (minterm & required_mask) == expected_bits
}

docs.title: Why Bitmask Conjunctions Outperform Standalone Regexes
docs.text:
1. Structural Context vs. Substring Matching: A benign user comment containing the words "script" and "character" activates isolated keyword flags, which causes probabilistic token scorers to produce false positives (24.6% FPR in our 1,000-request benchmark). In SATGuardian, rule SAT-XSS-01 requires the simultaneous presence of TAG_OPEN \(\land\) SCRIPT_ELEMENT \(\land\) DOM_EXEC, keeping the false positive rate below 0.1%.
  2. Predictable CPU Execution: Bitwise operations on a u128 register execute in a few CPU clock cycles without backtracking, preventing Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS).
  3. Human-Auditable Causal Traces: Every blocked request records the exact rule ID, active token set, and boolean clause in waf_ledger.db (e.g., (SELECT_PROJECTION AND UNION_CLAUSE) violates [SAT-SQLI-02] -> ACTION_BLOCK [sql_injection]).

docs.title: 4. Stage 3: Out-of-Band EXACTOR GXOR Boolean Minimization (src/cloud/satguardian_client.rs, exactor-core-v128)
docs.text:
When the Edge WAF encounters anomalous high-entropy requests or repeated hostile bursts that do not match an existing compiled cube, it logs the observed 128-bit minterm in the novel_anomalies table of waf_ledger.db.

Out of band, SatguardianCloudClient (src/cloud/satguardian_client.rs) and the Multi-Agent Advisor (satguardian-advisor.py) invoke the EXACTOR GXOR engine (procesar_gxor in exactor-core-v128) to compress these u128 minterms across up to 128 variables: 1. Differential Gray Code Mapping (modify_gray_code): Rather than performing exhaustive \(O(m^2)\) pairwise comparisons like classical Quine-McCluskey, EXACTOR projects u128 minterms into Gray Code space and locates logical neighbors in \(O(1)\) constant time via BTreeMap/HashMap lookups, achieving \(O(\text{term\_count})\) linear scaling. 2. GXOR / NXOR Algebraic Reduction over {AND, OR, NOT, XOR}: Classical {AND, OR, NOT} minimizers suffer from exponential clause explosion when simplifying symmetric, parity, or cross-dependent security predicates. EXACTOR GXOR detects exclusive-OR (XOR / NXOR) parity structures natively and reduces them into compact algebraic invariants over {AND, OR, NOT, XOR} up to 128 variables. 3. Digital Twin Replay (SimulationAgent): Before any synthesized rule is applied, satguardian-advisor.py tests the candidate bitmask against all historical benign requests stored in waf_ledger.db (1,663 benign requests in the current ledger) to verify < 0.1% false positives. 4. Atomic Hot-Reload (ArcSwap): Validated rules are compiled via compile_equation_to_clauses and hot-swapped into the running Rust Edge WAF via lock-free pointer replacement (ArcSwap) without dropping active TCP connections.

docs.text: Technical Evaluation Report Subject: Empirical Comparison of Signature-Based, Anomaly-Scoring, Semantic-Grammar, Probabilistic NLP, and Deterministic Bitmask WAF Engines Target System: satguardian (SATGuardian Edge WAF v0.2.0)

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary
docs.text:
This document presents a reproducible, empirical comparison between SATGuardian Edge WAF and four representative Web Application Firewall (WAF) architectures evaluated on the same hardware and attack dataset:

  1. SATGuardian Edge WAF (Native Rust & Python PoC Engine): Uses multi-pass lexical normalization (src/ast/lexer.rs), a 128-bit feature bitmask (FeatureVector in src/ast/features.rs), and bitwise rule evaluation ((minterm & required_mask) == expected_bits in src/engine/sat_solver.rs), paired with the out-of-band EXACTOR GXOR boolean minimizer (src/cloud/satguardian_client.rs \(\rightarrow\) exactor-core-v128) that simplifies up to 128 Boolean variables (u128) over {AND, OR, NOT, XOR}.
  2. Coraza WAF (OWASP CRS v4 Paranoia Level 1 Anomaly Scoring): Evaluates multi-target transformation pipelines (urlDecodeUni, htmlEntityDecode, replaceComments, compressWhitespace, lowercase) across 20 OWASP CRS v4 rules (920xxx–942xxx) accumulating an inbound anomaly score.
  3. SafeLine WAF (Chaitin T1K Semantic Grammar Ruleset): Applies single-pass URL/HTML decoding followed by lexical tokenization and semantic pattern matching across URI, query parameters, and request body.
  4. Probabilistic Token Scorer (Heuristic NLP Baseline): Computes character trigram distributions, Shannon entropy, and log-odds keyword weights to classify payloads probabilistically.
  5. Classical Regex WAF (ModSecurity CRS v3 Baseline): Scans raw HTTP request fields against unnormalized regular expression signatures.

docs.title: 3.1 SATGuardian vs. Coraza WAF (OWASP CRS v4 Anomaly Scoring)
docs.text:
• Latency (3.38x faster in Python, 15.0x faster in Native Rust): In OWASP CRS v4 Anomaly Scoring mode, Coraza must apply transformation pipelines (urlDecodeUni, htmlEntityDecode, replaceComments, compressWhitespace, lowercase) to each target variable (REQUEST_URI, ARGS, REQUEST_BODY, REQUEST_HEADERS) and evaluate all active rules without early exit to compute the total anomaly score (0.2178 ms avg). SATGuardian normalizes the payload in a single lexical pass and uses O(1) token surface guards and 128-bit integer bitwise masks, evaluating in 0.0644 ms in Python and 0.0145 ms (14.53 µs) in native Rust.
  • Detection Accuracy (99.9% capped vs. 97.3%): Standard CRS Paranoia Level 1 applies single-pass URL decoding (t:urlDecodeUni), which misses multi-encoded path traversal payloads (..%25252f..%25252fwindows%25252fwin.ini, resulting in a 5.4% FNR). Increasing CRS to Paranoia Level 3 or 4 catches multi-encoded payloads but significantly increases false positives on benign traffic. SATGuardian's iterative lexical decoder unwinds up to three nested encoding layers before extracting structural tokens.

docs.title: 3.2 SATGuardian vs. SafeLine WAF (Semantic Grammar)
docs.text:
• Latency (0.0644 ms vs. 0.0597 ms in Python; 0.0145 ms in Native Rust): SafeLine's single-pass semantic tokenizer is slightly faster in Python (0.0597 ms vs. 0.0644 ms) because it performs only one URL decode pass and does not generate LaTeX causal trace strings during evaluation. However, SATGuardian's native Rust implementation (0.0145 ms) is over 4x faster than the Python semantic baseline while generating full causal rule traces.
  • Detection Accuracy (99.9% capped vs. 94.4%): Because the baseline semantic grammar performs only single-pass decoding, double- and triple-encoded directory traversal vectors bypass inspection (11.2% FNR).

docs.title: 3.3 SATGuardian vs. Probabilistic Token Scorers (Heuristic NLP / ML Classifiers)
docs.text:
• False Positive Vulnerability (< 0.1% vs. 24.6% FPR): Probabilistic token-weight and character n-gram scorers assign positive threat weights to tokens like "script", "character", "select", and "python". When benign users submit comments such as "The script of the movie was great. I loved the character depth & direction!" or search for "How to learn SQL in 2026 & Python for Beginners", the cumulative log-odds score crosses the blocking threshold, causing a 24.6% false positive rate.
  • Structural Context in SATGuardian: SATGuardian requires conjunctions of structural tokens (e.g., TAG_OPEN \(\land\) SCRIPT_ELEMENT \(\land\) DOM_EXEC), allowing benign English prose containing technical keywords to pass without false positives (< 0.1% FPR).

docs.title: 3.4 SATGuardian vs. Classical Unnormalized Regex (ModSecurity CRS v3 Baseline)
docs.text: • Evasion Resilience (< 0.1% vs. 47.0% FNR): Scanning raw HTTP strings with traditional regex signatures is fast (0.0427 ms), but fails whenever attackers insert inline SQL comments (admin'/**/OR/**/1=1), URL-encode <script> tags (%3Cscript%3E), use SVG event handlers (<svg/onload=...>), or chain commands via subshells ($(curl ... | bash)), resulting in a 47.0% false negative rate.

docs.title: 1. Overview: Sub-Millisecond Sidecar Inspection
docs.text:
For high-throughput Kubernetes microservices and service meshes (Istio / Envoy), SATGuardian Edge WAF deploys as a lightweight, 100% self-contained native Rust sidecar container alongside each Envoy proxy pod.

Envoy delegates incoming HTTP request authorization to the local SATGuardian daemon via the ext_authz filter over an in-memory Unix Domain Socket (unix:///run/satguardian/waf.sock) or loopback gRPC/HTTP socket, avoiding external network hops.

docs.title: Why the Native Rust Sidecar Pattern Excels
docs.text:
1. Microsecond-Scale Engine Overhead: In empirical benchmarks (satguardian-waf-v0.2.0.exe benchmark -r 10000), the native Rust lexical and 128-bit bitmask engine evaluates requests in 13.60 µs median (p50) and 14.53 µs average (30.50 µs p99), keeping total sidecar authorization overhead well below Envoy's sub-millisecond SLA budget.
  2. 100% Traffic Sovereignty & Zero Per-Request Cost: All HTTP payloads stay strictly inside your Kubernetes cluster. There is zero external DNS CNAME routing, zero third-party traffic inspection, and $0.00 cost per request.
  3. Lock-Free Atomic Rule Updates (ArcSwap): When the offline advisor or SATGuardian Cloud synthesizes a minimized u128 rule matrix (consuming Security Units, SU), the sidecar hot-reloads the compiled bitmasks in memory via ArcSwap without restarting pods or dropping connections.
  4. Fail-Safe Continuity: If the organization's monthly Security Units (SU) balance is exhausted (HTTP 402 SU_QUOTA_EXHAUSTED), cloud rule synthesis pauses while every Kubernetes sidecar continues inspecting and blocking attacks indefinitely using its last compiled rule matrix.

docs.title: 2. Envoy ext_authz Configuration (envoy.yaml)
docs.text:
Configure Envoy's envoy.filters.http.ext_authz filter to forward request headers and bounded body payloads to the local SATGuardian sidecar:

http_filters:
  - name: envoy.filters.http.ext_authz
    typed_config:
      "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.ext_authz.v3.ExtAuthz
      transport_api_version: V3
      with_request_body:
        max_request_bytes: 8192
        allow_partial_message: true
        pack_as_bytes: true
      failure_mode_allow: false
      grpc_service:
        envoy_grpc:
          cluster_name: satguardian_ext_authz_cluster
        timeout: 0.05s

clusters:
  - name: satguardian_ext_authz_cluster
    type: STATIC
    connect_timeout: 0.01s
    typed_extension_protocol_options:
      envoy.extensions.upstreams.http.v3.HttpProtocolOptions:
        "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.upstreams.http.v3.HttpProtocolOptions
        explicit_http_config:
          http2_protocol_options: {}
    load_assignment:
      cluster_name: satguardian_ext_authz_cluster
      endpoints:
        - lb_endpoints:
            - endpoint:
                address:
                  pipe:
                    path: /run/satguardian/waf.sock

docs.title: 3. Kubernetes Deployment Manifest (k8s/envoy-sidecar-deployment.yaml)
docs.text:
Mount an in-memory emptyDir (medium: Memory) at /run/satguardian so Envoy and the satguardian-waf sidecar communicate over a shared RAM-backed Unix Domain Socket:

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: payment-api-protected
  labels:
    app: payment-api
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: payment-api
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: payment-api
    spec:
      volumes:
        - name: satguardian-uds
          emptyDir:
            medium: Memory
      containers:
        - name: satguardian-waf-sidecar
          image: ghcr.io/satguardian/satguardian-waf:v0.2.0
          args:
            - "proxy"
            - "--uds"
            - "/run/satguardian/waf.sock"
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: "100m"
              memory: "64Mi"
            limits:
              cpu: "500m"
              memory: "128Mi"
          volumeMounts:
            - name: satguardian-uds
              mountPath: /run/satguardian

        - name: envoy-front-proxy
          image: envoyproxy/envoy:v1.29-latest
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8080
          volumeMounts:
            - name: satguardian-uds

docs.title: Abstract
docs.text:
Modern Web Application Firewalls (WAFs) face a fundamental engineering tension between inspection latency, evasion resistance, and false positive rates. Traditional unnormalized regular expression engines execute quickly (0.0427 ms average in our Python benchmark) but fail against multi-layer URL encoding, inline SQL comments (/**/), and alternative DOM execution contexts (47.0% False Negative Rate). Conversely, full OWASP Core Rule Set (CRS v4) Anomaly Scoring engines apply multi-target transformations across dozens of rules per request (0.2178 ms average), while probabilistic NLP/token-weight classifiers suffer from high false positive rates (24.6% FPR) when benign requests contain technical terminology.

This paper presents the implemented architecture and empirical evaluation of SATGuardian Edge WAF (satguardian). SATGuardian decouples in-path request evaluation from out-of-band boolean rule minimization: 1. In-Path Hot Plane (Native Rust): Applies bounded multi-pass lexical normalization (src/ast/lexer.rs), packs structural tokens and request attributes into a 128-bit integer (FeatureVector(pub u128) in src/ast/features.rs), and evaluates compiled rule cubes via single-cycle bitwise operations ((minterm & required_mask) == expected_bits in src/engine/sat_solver.rs). Across 10,000 requests, the compiled Rust engine achieves a median latency (p50) of 13.60 µs (0.0136 ms), a mean latency of 14.53 µs (0.0145 ms), and a p99 of 30.50 µs (65,441.13 req/sec single-thread throughput). 2. Out-of-Band Synthesis Plane (Rust & Python): Logs novel anomalous u128 minterms to a local SQLite ledger (waf_ledger.db), simplifies up to 128 Boolean variables asynchronously using the EXACTOR GXOR engine (src/cloud/satguardian_client.rs \(\rightarrow\) exactor-core-v128) over the complete {AND, OR, NOT, XOR} operator basis via Differential Gray Code Mapping, verifies < 0.1% false positives against historical benign traffic in a Digital Twin (satguardian-advisor.py), and hot-reloads the compiled bitmasks via lock-free ArcSwap.

docs.title: 1.1 Lexical Normalization & Feature Vector Mapping
docs.text:
Let an incoming HTTP request be represented by the tuple \(r = (M, P, Q, H, B)\) denoting method, path, query string, headers, and body.

The lexical normalizer \(\mathcal{N}\) (src/ast/lexer.rs) applies bounded iterative percent-decoding (\(k \le 3\) passes) and inline comment stripping (/*...*/) to produce a canonical byte stream \(s = \mathcal{N}(r)\), from which it extracts a set of structural tokens \(\mathcal{T}(s)\) and maps \(r\) into a 128-bit boolean feature vector:

\[\mathbf{v}(r) \in \{0, 1\}^{128} \quad (\text{represented in Rust as } \texttt{u128})\]

Each bit \(v_i \in \{0, 1\}\) (\(i \in \{0, \dots, 127\}\)) encodes a deterministic predicate (e.g., presence of SQL tautology tokens, UNION SELECT projection, executable <script> or inline DOM event attributes, shell command chaining operators, relative path traversal sequences, or high character Shannon entropy \(H(s) > \tau\)).

docs.title: 1.2 In-Path Bitmask Cube Evaluation (src/engine/sat_solver.rs)
docs.text:
Each compiled security rule \(c_j\) is a boolean cube (product term / conjunction of literals) represented by two 128-bit integers: - required_mask (\(M_j \in \texttt{u128}\)): Bitmask indicating which of the 128 variables participate in rule \(j\). - expected_bits (\(E_j \in \texttt{u128}\)): Expected polarity (1 for positive literal, 0 for negated literal) of those active variables.

At runtime, evaluating whether request \(\mathbf{v}(r)\) triggers rule \(c_j\) requires a single bitwise AND and equality check:

\[\text{Match}(\mathbf{v}(r), c_j) \iff (\mathbf{v}(r) \mathbin{\&} M_j) == E_j\]

If no rule cube matches (\(\forall j, \, (\mathbf{v}(r) \mathbin{\&} M_j) \neq E_j\)), the security invariant holds and the request is allowed. Unlike backtracking regular expressions or NP-complete in-path DPLL/CDCL solvers, bitwise evaluation over \(R\) rules executes in deterministic \(O(R)\) CPU cycles.

docs.title: 1.3 Out-of-Band EXACTOR GXOR Minimization (src/cloud/satguardian_client.rs, exactor-core-v128)
docs.text: When unobserved malicious minterms \(\mathcal{M} = \{m_1, m_2, \dots, m_k\} \subset \{0, 1\}^{n}\) (\(n \le 128\)) are collected in waf_ledger.db, classical {AND, OR, NOT} minimizers (such as Quine-McCluskey or Espresso) suffer from \(O(2^n)\) exponential blow-up beyond 20–30 variables. Instead, the out-of-band synthesizer invokes the EXACTOR GXOR engine (procesar_gxor in exactor-core-v128) via SatguardianCloudClient::simplify: 1. Differential Gray Code Mapping (modify_gray_code): Projects 128-bit minterms into a Gray Code space and locates logical neighbors differing by a single bit (\(\text{popcount}(E_a \oplus E_b) = 1\)) in \(O(1)\) constant time via BTreeMap/HashMap lookups, achieving \(O(\text{term\_count})\) linear complexity: $\(M_{\text{merged}} = M_a \mathbin{\&} \neg(E_a \oplus E_b), \quad E_{\text{merged}} = E_a \mathbin{\&} M_{\text{merged}}\)$ 2. GXOR / NXOR Algebraic Reduction over {AND, OR, NOT, XOR}: Detects exclusive-OR (\(\oplus\)) and equivalence (\(\odot\)) structures across up to 128 Boolean variables (u128), collapsing parity and symmetric attack predicates that would otherwise require exponentially many Sum-of-Products (SOP) clauses. 3. Digital Twin Verification (satguardian-advisor.py): Before adding any reduced invariant \(c^*\) to the active rule matrix, the SimulationAgent verifies that \(c^*\) produces < 0.1% false positives across the historical benign set \(\mathcal{B}_{\text{ledger}}\) (1,663 benign requests in waf_ledger.db).

1. Latency Comparison (Native Rust vs. Python vs. CRS Anomaly Scoring):
  2. The native Rust engine (satguardian-waf-v0.2.0.exe) evaluates 10,000 requests in 0.1528 s (13.60 µs median, 14.53 µs mean, 30.50 µs p99), which is 4.4x faster than the Python reference implementation (64.40 µs mean) and 15.0x faster than Coraza OWASP CRS v4 Anomaly Scoring (217.80 µs mean).

  4. False Negative Analysis (Multi-Layer Encoding Evasions):
  5. Classical Unnormalized Regex (47.0% FNR): Fails on inline SQL comments (admin'/**/OR/**/1=1), URL-encoded <script> tags (%3Cscript%3E), SVG event handlers (<svg/onload=...>), subshell expansions ($(...)), and double-encoded path traversal (..%252f..%252f).
  6. SafeLine T1K Semantic Grammar (11.2% FNR) & Coraza CRS PL1 (5.4% FNR): Single-pass URL decoding (t:urlDecodeUni) catches single-encoded attacks but misses triple URL-encoded path traversal (..%25252f..%25252fwindows%25252fwin.ini). SATGuardian's 3-pass conditional URL decoder resolves nested encodings before tokenizing.
  7. False Positive Analysis (Benign Technical Prose):
  8. Probabilistic Token Scorer (24.6% FPR): Assigns additive log-odds weights to tokens like "script", "character", and "select". Benign user comments such as "The script of the movie was great. I loved the character depth & direction!" cross the anomaly threshold and are falsely blocked.
  9. SATGuardian Bitmask Conjunctions (< 0.1% FPR): Requires structural conjunctions (TAG_OPEN \(\land\) SCRIPT_ELEMENT \(\land\) DOM_EXEC), allowing benign technical prose to pass cleanly.
